display.title: Mayerke: A Boy Who Would Not Eat Treif
display.summary_short: Hidden with a Russian family during the war, ten-year-old Mayerke refuses all non-kosher food through hunger and beatings, until he and his mother find each other again.
display.summary_long: As the German army advances on their Russian city, Mrs. Levin leaves her ten-year-old son Mayerke with a kind non-Jewish childhood friend, Nastya, and flees into hiding. Her last words to him: remember you are a Jew, eat only kosher, and keep Shabbos. Renamed Misha Sedov, Mayerke lives on fruit and vegetables and will not touch the family's soup. Nastya's husband Fedya, a drunkard, declares war on the stubborn boy, beating him and trying to force-feed him, yet Mayerke holds firm until even Fedya is afraid of his strength. When the fighting returns, the family flees to crowded Sverdlovsk, where Mayerke refuses even a precious glass of milk because it is not chalav Yisroel. After the war his mother searches the ruins of her street and asks the tzaddik Reb Wolf for a blessing; he promises she will find her son quickly if he has kept himself from treif. Mayerke sets off alone to find her just as she arrives in Sverdlovsk, and a group of war orphans' teasing song about a boy who eats only cucumbers leads her straight to him.
display.lesson: Keeping kosher is a deep bond between a Jew and Hashem; if a child could keep it with such mesiras nefesh, we who live in peace can surely learn Torah and do mitzvos with joy.

advisories.note: Set during the German invasion of Russia in World War II: bombing, shooting, people killed, war orphans.
A drunk man beats a ten-year-old and tries to force non-kosher food into his mouth.
The foster uncle comes home drunk every week and rages.
A fatherless boy separated from his mother for the whole war, hungry and alone; happy reunion.

sources_cited.note: 'As the Rebbe shlita has told us many times': today we are asked only to learn Torah and do mitzvos in peace.

segments.title: Mayerke and the kosher food
segments.summary: A Jewish boy hidden with a Russian family during the war refuses all treif and is reunited with his mother.

segments.title: Mesiras nefesh in our times
segments.summary: The storyteller explains that today all we are asked is to learn Torah and do mitzvos in peace.
